caption:
that feeling that you're faking it and someone's about to find out?

it has a name. and it shows up in the people you'd least expect.

when do you feel it most? 👇

slides.text:
if you feel like a fraud
read this
slides.image: hooded man shadow gym identity mask

slides.result: First described in 1978 by psychologists Pauline Clance and Suzanne Imes, in **high-achieving women** who believed they weren't as capable as others thought.
slides.source: Clance & Imes, Psychotherapy: Theory, Research & Practice (1978)

slides.result: A review of 62 studies found rates anywhere from **9% to 82%,** depending on the group.
slides.source: Bravata et al., Journal of General Internal Medicine (2020)

slides.text:
it was first found in people
who were already succeeding

feeling like a fraud isn't proof you are one
sometimes it means you're growing
slides.image: shadow self overhead runner long shadow

slides.text:
the feeling doesn't leave first
you go first
slides.image: silhouette in window frame freedom breaking out
